title: Planning Commission Hearing
text: A federal planning commission has scheduled a hearing on your ballroom. Forty slides on setbacks, sightlines and stormwater. None have a chandelier.

options.label: Sit through all forty slides
options.result: The design was reviewed. Slide 31 was about drainage. You now know about drainage.

ignore.text: The ballroom plans went unreviewed. The commission has sent a strongly worded calendar invite.

inspiredBy: The planning commission took up the ballroom design in the fall of 2025, after demolition began.

title: Historical Association Briefing
text: The White House Historical Association explains, with binders, which rooms are historic and why they were not supposed to vanish.

options.label: Read the binders
options.result: You learned the East Wing had a history. It was mostly offices. Nobody enjoyed this.

ignore.text: The binder was left on a radiator. The association is drafting a longer binder.

inspiredBy: Historians and the White House Historical Association objected to the East Wing demolition in October 2025.

title: Memorial Circle Traffic Study
text: Engineers brief you on how a 250-foot arch affects traffic at Memorial Circle. They have a lot of arrows.

options.label: Study the arrows
options.result: Westbound lanes will narrow. The arch will not honk, but everyone else will.

ignore.text: Commuters learned about the arch from a detour sign. They had notes.

inspiredBy: Federal planning documents in 2026 described traffic changes around the proposed arch at Memorial Circle.

title: Cost Overrun Review
text: A contractor walks you through a ballroom budget that grew from a number to a larger number. Spreadsheets have color-coded tabs.

options.label: Review every tab
options.result: The tabs were red. The total was a mystery. You approved a footnote.

ignore.text: Nobody reviewed the budget. It reviewed itself and grew.

inspiredBy: Reported ballroom cost estimates rose through late 2025 and 2026, well beyond early figures.

title: Kennedy Center Facilities Review
text: A facilities manager presents the Kennedy Center boiler, roof and elevator schedule. The boiler has no opinion on your name.

options.label: Learn the boiler schedule
options.result: The roof leaks in six places. None are the sign. This is a minor mercy.

ignore.text: The roof held a meeting of its own and leaked on a rehearsal.

inspiredBy: The Kennedy Center board and administration discussed renovation and renaming through late 2025 and 2026.

title: Secret Service Construction Briefing
text: Security staff explain what must go under, around and inside a large new White House building. It is a lot of concrete and no gold.

options.label: Accept the concrete
options.result: Security is satisfied. The basement is secret, which is the best kind of basement.

ignore.text: The security plan was skipped. The building will be constructed on optimism.

inspiredBy: Reports in 2025 said the ballroom project included extensive security and underground work.

title: A Demolition Permit Question
text: A contractor asks if the wall in front of him needs a permit before it is removed. Several walls are already gone.

options.label: File the review first
options.result: Reviews are paperwork. Gone is gone. The contractor files it after, and so does your pride.

options.label: Tell him to swing away
options.result: The wall fell with great ceremony. The paperwork arrived at its own funeral.

ignore.text: The wall stayed up until a deadline passed. The contractor napped on a pallet.

inspiredBy: The East Wing was demolished in October 2025, with review questions following afterward.

title: Fine Arts Commission Vacancies
text: The Commission of Fine Arts needs members who will read the designs. Your list has people who just like gold.

options.label: Appoint actual architects
options.result: The new members ask about proportion. A chandelier is shown a chair.

options.label: Appoint your favorite fans
options.result: Approval arrived in nine minutes. A cornice cried a little.

ignore.text: The commission lacked a quorum. A fountain went unreviewed and rejoiced.

inspiredBy: The Commission of Fine Arts was reshaped in 2025 after members were dismissed.

title: A Preservation Lawsuit
text: Preservationists have sued over the ballroom and want a judge to review the process. Your lawyers want to settle the schedule.

options.label: Cooperate with the court
options.result: You attended the hearing. A judge asked about process. Process answered, sort of.

options.label: Tell the court it is a beautiful ballroom
options.result: The court noted it was beautiful and also a lawsuit. These are different things.

ignore.text: The deadline passed. The lawsuit grew a second exhibit of photographs.

inspiredBy: The National Trust for Historic Preservation sued over the ballroom project in late 2025.

title: The Donor List
text: Ethics staff ask for a list of who is paying for the ballroom. The donors prefer to appear in a large golden acknowledgment.

options.label: Publish the donor list
options.result: The list was published. Several companies suddenly love transparency, in a small font.

options.label: Put donors on a gold plaque
options.result: The plaque is huge. Ethics staff counted the names and then counted other things.

ignore.text: The list stayed secret. A conspiracy theorist emailed a spreadsheet of yachts.

inspiredBy: Corporate and individual donors to the ballroom were disclosed in part in October 2025.

title: A Question About Sightlines
text: Veterans say a 250-foot arch would block the view between Arlington House and the Lincoln Memorial. They have a diagram.

options.label: Commission a sightline study
options.result: The study says the view is a view. It recommends not building in the middle of it.

options.label: Declare the arch the new view
options.result: The arch is now the view. The Lincoln Memorial looks away.

ignore.text: The veterans filed in court. The arch has a new, damp diagram.

inspiredBy: Vietnam veterans sued in early 2026 to block the proposed Memorial Circle arch over sightlines.

title: Humanities Funding Request
text: A grant officer asks if humanities money should fund an arch or the usual libraries, archives and museums.

options.label: Fund the archives
options.result: Three archives got money. One is a librarian who has never seen gold paint.

options.label: Fund the arch
options.result: The arch got fifteen million. A poet received a very kind thank-you note.

ignore.text: The grant officer waited. The archives got a bake sale.

inspiredBy: A 2026 NEH spending plan reportedly set aside about $15 million for the arch project.

title: The Ethics Form
text: An ethics lawyer has a gift disclosure form for a very large aircraft. The form has a box labeled foreign government.

options.label: Fill the form out properly
options.result: You filled it. The box was checked. A lawyer smiled for the first time this year.

options.label: Write great plane in the box
options.result: The form was returned with notes. The notes are mostly in red.

ignore.text: The form sat unfilled. An aircraft awaits in a hangar, quietly judged.

inspiredBy: The Qatari jet offered in May 2025 drew Emoluments Clause questions and disclosure demands.

title: The Ethics Office Vacancy
text: The government ethics office needs a director who will review your gifts. Candidates are boring and frightening.

options.label: Appoint a qualified reviewer
options.result: The reviewer asked for receipts. Everyone remembered what receipts are.

options.label: Appoint a loyal friend
options.result: The new director found no issue. The old director found a cardboard box.

ignore.text: The ethics post stayed vacant. Conflicts of interest enjoyed the open desk.

inspiredBy: The head of the Office of Government Ethics was removed in early 2025.

title: The Giant Banner
text: Staff ask whether a huge portrait banner can hang on a federal building. Facilities staff ask who pays for the ladder.

options.label: Keep the facade clean
options.result: The facade is a facade again. A flag is back and quietly jubilant.

options.label: Order a banner five stories tall
options.result: You are now the tallest thing on Constitution Avenue. Pigeons complain.

ignore.text: No banner, no response. A department head has rolled up a hallway carpet.

inspiredBy: Large presidential portrait banners appeared on federal buildings in 2025.

title: Oval Office Gold Order
text: A decorator asks whether the Oval Office has enough gold. The curator, standing by the wall, appears to be dying inside.

options.label: Keep the room historic
options.result: The room is fine. The decorator is grieving in the hall, among the swatches.

options.label: Add a gold cherub and more gold
options.result: The room now looks like a very rich dentist found a time machine.

ignore.text: Nobody decided. The room slowly gained gold anyway, per the law of drift.

inspiredBy: The Oval Office gained extensive gold ornamentation in 2025.

title: Rose Garden Paving Plan
text: The grounds crew wants to know whether the Rose Garden may remain a garden. A paver salesman is already in the room.

options.label: Keep the roses
options.result: The roses stay. The grounds crew cries a little, then waters them.

options.label: Pave it for parties
options.result: The garden is now a patio. The roses are a rumor and a table decoration.

ignore.text: The roses waited. A salesman stood in the beds, with a sample tile.

inspiredBy: The Rose Garden was converted to a paved patio in 2025.

title: Who Is Paying?
text: A reporter asks who is funding the ballroom, and whether they received anything in return. Several donors are suddenly in the hall.

options.label: Give the full answer
options.result: A donor list, a number, a date. The press room is startled by a complete sentence.

options.label: Say it is all very generous
options.result: Everyone is generous. The reporter writes down generous. And a question mark.

ignore.text: The question hung in the room. A donor took the hint and also left.

inspiredBy: Reporters pressed the administration over ballroom donors in October 2025.

title: The East Wing Question
text: A reporter asks why the East Wing was demolished when you said it would not be touched. The answer you gave was a photograph of a hole.

options.label: Acknowledge the change
options.result: You said plans changed. This is the most truthful thing a demolition has ever produced.

options.label: Say it was always the plan
options.result: There was a plan. There was also a hole. The two did not meet.

ignore.text: You skipped it. The reporter described the hole for six minutes.

inspiredBy: Trump had said the ballroom would not touch the East Wing, then it was demolished in October 2025.

title: Kennedy Center Name Question
text: A reporter asks who approved adding your name to the Kennedy Center, and whether Congress has any say. The statute is on a lectern.

options.label: Say Congress decides
options.result: You cited the statute. The statute looked flattered and also nervous.

options.label: Say the board loves you
options.result: The board loved you in a unanimous voice. The statute filed a motion.

ignore.text: The reporter turned to a page of law. It was long.

inspiredBy: The Kennedy Center board voted in December 2025 to add the president's name, despite a statute naming it for another president.

title: The Coin Question
text: A reporter asks whether a commemorative coin with a living president on it is allowed. A numismatist is hiding under the table.

options.label: Say you will check the law
options.result: You checked. The law says living people do not go on coins. You went quiet.

options.label: Say the coin is already minted
options.result: The coin is a handsome coin. Legal says it is the first of a series called Trouble.

ignore.text: The question lingered. A coin collector fainted into a velvet tray.

inspiredBy: A 2026 semiquincentennial coin design featuring the sitting president drew legal and ethical scrutiny.

title: The Arch Height Question
text: A reporter asks if the arch is taller than the Arc de Triomphe. You have a numerical answer and a large ego.

options.label: Cite the official height
options.result: The height is official. The reporter asked a follow-up about the angel. A pause fell.

options.label: Say it is the biggest arch ever
options.result: It is the biggest arch ever, in a sense your architect said not to say.

ignore.text: The reporter measured the room instead, with a tape.

inspiredBy: Renderings unveiled in April 2026 showed a roughly 250-foot arch topped with a statue.

title: The Merchandise Question
text: A reporter asks whether selling products with your name while in office is a conflict. A hat vendor is waving at the cameras.

options.label: Promise a careful review
options.result: The review is careful. The hats are available wherever hats are sold.

options.label: Say the hats are patriotic
options.result: The hats are patriotic. The reporter is wearing one. The reporter is troubled by that.

ignore.text: The question hung. The hat vendor took a bow.

inspiredBy: Trump-branded merchandise and licensing deals continued during his second term in 2025.

title: Tour Group Complaint
text: A tour group arrives to find the East Wing gone and the gift shop entrance a construction site. The group has a guide and a grievance.

options.label: Apologize and reroute them
options.result: The tour was rerouted. A child asked where the wing went. Nobody had a good answer.

options.label: Wave and sign their hats
options.result: They loved it, and also did not see the wing. The guide is looking for a new job.

ignore.text: The tour group waited at a fence. The fence was very patient.

inspiredBy: Public tours and the East Wing visitor entrance were disrupted by the 2025 demolition and construction.

title: The Architect Calls
text: The ballroom architect has a question about whether the load-bearing walls can be removed. They are load-bearing.

options.label: Ask her to keep them
options.result: She kept them. A civil engineer wept with joy, a lone figure in the dust.

options.label: Say gravity is negotiable
options.result: Gravity declined to comment. The architect moved the call to a more stable room.

ignore.text: The architect waited. The walls waited. The walls are better at it.

inspiredBy: Architects and engineers worked on the ballroom design amid shifting plans in 2025 and 2026.

title: Preservation Board Chair
text: The chair of a preservation board wants a public hearing before you rename a historic building. She has a gavel and a deep calm.

options.label: Agree to the hearing
options.result: You agreed. She banged the gavel once and it was the nicest sound you heard all week.

options.label: Rename it by Friday
options.result: It was renamed by Friday. A plaque went up. A lawsuit went up faster.

ignore.text: The chair held the hearing anyway. The empty chair was thoroughly examined.

inspiredBy: Preservation officials questioned renaming and construction moves in Washington throughout 2025 and 2026.

title: A Donor Phones In
text: A large donor has an idea for naming the ballroom after himself, or perhaps you. He wants it in writing.

options.label: Say naming goes through ethics
options.result: He was disappointed. The ethics office was elated and did a small dance.

options.label: Name it after him, or you
options.result: The two of you spent an hour on naming. The ballroom is still a hole.

ignore.text: The donor left a voicemail. It was long, and mostly about plaques.

inspiredBy: Donors to the ballroom were reported in 2025 to include major corporations and wealthy individuals.

title: The Contractor Calls
text: The contractor says the gold plating will not fit the budget or the wall. She would like a decision about either.

options.label: Choose the cheaper finish
options.result: She chose paint. The wall is happy and the budget is moderately sedated.

options.label: Insist on the gold plating
options.result: The gold is going on. The budget is going elsewhere, to the lawn, to weep.

ignore.text: The contractor kept going. The finish is a surprise to everyone.

inspiredBy: Gold finishes and heavy decor were added to White House rooms through 2025.

title: An Artist Cancels
text: A Kennedy Center performer calls to say she is canceling because of the new name. She is polite and very firm.

options.label: Thank her and move on
options.result: You took it politely. Another performer was booked. The house is still full.

options.label: Tell her she is fired
options.result: She cannot be fired from a show she canceled. The headline wrote itself.

ignore.text: The performer left a voicemail. The orchestra took a vote.

inspiredBy: Several artists canceled Kennedy Center appearances after the board added the president's name in late 2025.

title: The Naval Shipyard Calls
text: A shipyard manager asks whether ships should be named after the president or a more traditional hero. He has a drawing.

options.label: Pick the traditional name
options.result: The ship will be named for a hero. A lot of sailors quietly saluted.

options.label: Name it after yourself
options.result: The ship is yours. It has gold trim. It is also not yet built.

ignore.text: The shipyard waited. The ship is nameless and slightly offended.

inspiredBy: The administration floated large new warships under a "Trump-class" label in late 2025.
